label: Formulated the sociological concept of Asabiyyah
description: Ibn Khaldun conceptualized Asabiyyah (group feeling / social cohesion) as the fundamental engine of political rise, state formation, and inevitable dynastic decay.
historicalContext: Articulated in the Muqaddimah (1377) during his retreat at the castle of Ibn Salama in modern Algeria after decades observing political turbulence across North Africa and Al-Andalus.
dialecticalTension: Contrasts the robust, egalitarian solidarity of rural nomadic life with the enervating, corrupting luxury of sedentary urban civilization.

citations.author: Ibn Khaldun
citations.work: The Muqaddimah: An Introduction to History
citations.quote: Royal authority and dynasties can only be established through group feeling (Asabiyyah). When luxury corrupts group feeling, the dynasty falls.

citations.author: Franz Rosenthal
citations.work: The Muqaddimah: An Introduction to History (Translation and Introduction)

label: Applied Aristotelian naturalism to social history
description: Ibn Khaldun transformed Aristotle's premise that humans are social and political animals by nature into an empirical science of human civilization (Ilm al-Umran).
historicalContext: Trained in the Maghrebi Aristotelian tradition, Ibn Khaldun sought natural, material causes for historical transformations rather than mythological explanations.
dialecticalTension: Extended teleological biological maturation and decay to political institutions and social structures.

citations.author: Ibn Khaldun
citations.quote: Human society is necessary. The philosophers express this by saying that man is political by nature.

label: Inherited Andalusian rationalist historiography
description: Ibn Khaldun adopted Averroes' rationalist critique of unverified narrative traditions, applying dialectical scrutiny to historical reporting and causal analysis.
historicalContext: The intellectual heritage of Averroistic rationalism survived in the Maghrebi courts where Ibn Khaldun served as jurist and chancellor.
dialecticalTension: Shifted Averroistic metaphysics toward an empirical and sociological study of human association.

citations.author: Ibn Khaldun
citations.quote: The inner meaning of history involves speculation and an attempt to touch the truth, subtle explanation of the causes and origins of existing things.

label: Anticipated empirical sociology and social physics
description: Ibn Khaldun is recognized as the first thinker to formulate an autonomous science of society governed by universal laws, prefiguring Comte's social physics and sociology.
historicalContext: 19th-century European orientalists and sociologists, reading de Slane's French translation of the Muqaddimah, recognized Ibn Khaldun as the precursor to positive sociology.
dialecticalTension: Constructed a science of social laws centuries before the European Enlightenment positivist movement.

citations.author: Ludwig Gumplowicz
citations.quote: A pious Muslim took in all seriousness the study of the laws of human society that Auguste Comte later formulated as sociology.

label: Anticipated materialist and economic cycles of history
description: Ibn Khaldun's analysis of labor value, division of labor, surplus value, and economic cycles directly prefigured core tenets of historical materialism.
historicalContext: The Muqaddimah's chapters on crafts, commerce, and state taxation analyze social institutions as downstream consequences of production and material subsistence.
dialecticalTension: Identified economic modes of production as the material foundation of social and political structures.

citations.author: Ibn Khaldun
citations.quote: Man obtains his sustenance and profit through labor. Without human labor, no profit or capital can be acquired.

citations.author: Yves Lacoste
citations.work: Ibn Khaldun: The Birth of History and the Past of the Third World
